video.title: I Helped a Subscriber to Build an App in 24 Hours

summary: Mikey No Code documents building a custom client-tracking app in Base44 for Priya, a one-person interior styling business (Willow Lane Interiors, Manchester), within 24 hours of her community post. The video focuses on scoping: workflow interviews, a one-sentence goal, prioritising four version-one features and parking five, then a single complete build prompt with a visual direction and avoid list. Feedback was routed via AI-generated client questions and screenshots in discussion mode, and real-day use exposed a missing required follow-up date. Key takeaway: with AI builders, deciding what not to build is the hard part.

tactics.name: Workflow-first discovery instead of feature lists
steps: Ask the owner to walk through the business from first inquiry to finished job, including annoying parts
Ask who will use the app and the one recent problem they wish hadn't happened
Have them finish one sentence: what the app should keep in one place and why
Use that sentence as the rule: features that serve it stay, others are parked

quote.text: rather than asking her what features she wanted, we started somewhere much more useful
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Monday-morning prioritisation
steps: Ask which feature they'd miss first if it wasn't there on Monday morning
Order version one by the answers
Park features with a reason (invoicing, auto emails, client portal, calendar sync, multiple logins)

quote.text: We asked her which thing she would miss first if she opened up the app on Monday morning and they weren't there
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: One complete build prompt with an avoid list
steps: Describe business, single user, the core question the app answers
Specify fields, pipeline stages, money and follow-up logic and the only screens allowed
Give a concrete visual direction and an explicit avoid list (no purple/blue gradients, dark mode, glassy cards, stock illustrations)
Ask for 12 realistic sample clients across all stages

quote.text: describing what you do not want is one of the most reliable ways to stop an AI-generated app from falling back into the same default look
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Let the AI generate client questions
steps: After the first build, ask Base44 to list the 3-4 decisions it had to guess
Turn them into plain-language questions for the client
Screenshot client replies and paste into Base44 discussion mode
Agree the plan before applying changes

quote.text: identify the three or four decisions it had been forced to guess at
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Polished handoff
steps: Rename the app URL to the business name
Confirm it works on the client's phone
Run the security scan before handing over

quote.text: A random URL still feels like something you're testing
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Building the final version on day one causes overwhelm and abandoned projects.

quote.text: someone tries to build the final version on day one, adds everything they can think of, gets overwhelmed
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: The requested feature is often a symptom: a reminders tool would have become a fourth place to check.

quote.text: A separate reminder tool would have simply just become a fourth place to check
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Unstated requirements (e.g. making follow-up date compulsory) only surface in real use.

quote.text: we simply never told it that a follow-up date had to be required
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Adding features one prompt at a time makes AI builders guess at structure.
Renaming a Base44 URL kills the old address immediately.

lessons.lesson: Understand the workflow before talking software; the first ask is usually a symptom.

quote.text: the first thing someone asks an app to solve is often only the symptom
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Fit the app to the client's existing process so they keep using it; off-the-shelf CRMs force change and get abandoned.
Scope is the bottleneck when AI makes building fast.

quote.text: deciding what not to build becomes the hardest part of the whole job
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Real-day usage finds bugs a demo click-through never will.

quote.text: there was almost no chance we would have caught that just by clicking through the screens once after the build
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Show money values, not counts, on pipeline views for small businesses.
Small handoff touches (branded URL) make a build feel like a real product.
Use AI builders' discussion/plan mode before changes to avoid unrequested redesigns.
